summary: Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1953), Harvard College (~1953–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl Georg Zistl was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1904–1910) under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a wissenschaftlicher Hilfsarbeiter at Munich University Library from 1911 to 1952.
Karl Gottlieb Ewald Rhenius worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Berlin Mission Seminary in 1810 and served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society from around 1814 to 1835.

Karl Graul was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied theology at the University of Leipzig in 1834. He served as director of the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission (1844–1860) and taught Missionswissenschaft at Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1861.

Karl H. Potter, an Indologist and philosopher, earned degrees from UC Berkeley and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Carleton College, the University of Minnesota, and the University of Washington, and edited the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies.

Karl Hoffmann was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Walther Wüst. He held positions at Munich, Saarland University, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, where he held the chair for comparative Indo-European and Indo-Iranian philology (1955–1983).

Karl Hummel was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Munich under Wilhelm Geiger and studied at Tübingen under Enno Littmann. He was a botany assistant and director at Tübingen (1946–1976), and a visiting professor at Tehran.

Karl Jahn worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. After earning his PhD under Moriz Winternitz at Charles University, he taught at the German University in Prague, Utrecht University (1950–1972), and Leiden University (1953–1973).
Karl Jaspers was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University (~1902–1909) and later served on the faculty there from around 1913 to 1948.

Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna and held posts at the Museum of Ethnology Vienna, University of Vienna, Mainz, and Heidelberg (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann was an Indologist and philosopher. After studying at Mainz and Würzburg, he served as professor at the Gymnasium and Lyceum in Aschaffenburg, Hofbibliothekar at the Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg, and professor at the University of Bonn from 1818.
Karl Lachmann was a linguist who studied at the universities of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.
Karl Marx was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Bonn, Berlin, and Jena. He held posts with the Rheinische Zeitung (~1842–1843) and the Neue Rheinische Zeitung (~1848–1849).
Karl Müllenhoff was a linguist and historian who studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Leipzig. He held academic posts at Kiel University (1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (1858).

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, taught at the Magdalenaeum Wrocław, and served as professor of eloquence at the University of Göttingen from 1819 until 1840.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Reinhardt was a philosopher who studied at Bonn and Berlin under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held university posts at Bonn (~1914–1918), Hamburg (~1919–1923), Frankfurt (~1924–1946), and Leipzig (~1946–1951).

Karl Richard Lepsius was an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin under August Boeckh. He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute at Rome, Humboldt University of Berlin, Egyptian Museum of Berlin, and Prussian State Library.

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, Heidelberg, and Halle. He held a chair of philosophy at the University of Halle (~1830–1833) before becoming professor and rector at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Schenkl worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna, studied under Georg Curtius, and held professorships in classical philology at Innsbruck (1857–1864), Graz (1864–1875), and the University of Vienna (1875–1899).
